articles.title: Speculative Decoding in vLLM: EAGLE, MTP, and Draft Models — When Drafting Pays and When It Costs
articles.excerpt: Your 70B model generates one token per forward pass. Each pass reads all 140 GB of weights from GPU memory while the arithmetic units sit mostly idle — decode is memory-bound, not compute-bound. Check…
articles.body: Your 70B model generates one token per forward pass. Each pass reads all 140 GB of weights from GPU memory while the arithmetic units sit mostly idle — decode is memory-bound, not compute-bound. Checking five candidate tokens in one pass costs barely more than checking one, because the weights are read once either way. Speculative decoding exploits exactly that: a cheap drafter guesses the next few tokens, the big model verifies them all in a single pass, and you keep the longest prefix it agrees with. Done right, it is a 2–3x speedup with zero change to the output distribution. Done wrong, it is a second model burning GPU time to produce tokens you throw away.

articles.title: Stop Turning Your Daily Scrum Into a 15-Minute Status Report
articles.excerpt: The Daily Scrum is a Tactical Huddle, Not a Status Update If your developers are staring at their screens, waiting for their turn to speak, and reporting their activities directly to the Scrum Master,…
articles.body: The Daily Scrum is a Tactical Huddle, Not a Status Update If your developers are staring at their screens, waiting for their turn to speak, and reporting their activities directly to the Scrum Master, your standup is fundamentally broken. The Daily Scrum is not a micro-management status report. It is a 15-minute tactical huddle specifically for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their daily plan. I see development teams get this wrong constantly. They treat the event as a daily roll call. Developer A recites a Jira ticket number. Developer B mumbles about being in meetings all day. The Scrum Master checks a box, and everyone goes back to working in complete isolation. This kills momentum, masks critical blockers, and destroys team cohesion.

articles.title: Verifying the CVE-2026-123633 fix across packages and running workers
articles.excerpt: Verifying the CVE-2026-123633 fix across packages and running workers A patch ticket can close before the vulnerable worker stops running. CVE-2026-123633 makes that gap visible because NGINX may sit…
articles.body: Verifying the CVE-2026-123633 fix across packages and running workers A patch ticket can close before the vulnerable worker stops running. CVE-2026-123633 makes that gap visible because NGINX may sit behind a distribution package, a container image, or a bundled commercial product. Vulnerability overview F5 advisory K000163928 describes a use-after-free in ngx_http_v2_module . The flaw is CWE-416, with CVSS v3.1 8.1 and CVSS v4.0 9.2. F5 lists denial of service and possible code execution; the latter depends on ASLR being disabled or bypassed. NGINX Open Source 1.19.7 through 1.31.8 is affected. The fixed upstream releases are 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. NGINX Plus branches have separate fixed point releases, and several bundled products have their own patch rows.
articles.author: OnaEiuspkz

articles.title: Your alert fires at 75% failure. The freeze lawsuit is asking why anyone should wait that long.
articles.excerpt: Quick audit you can run today: find an alert in your stack that only fires when a huge share of things fail. That alert is not monitoring. It is a decision, made by a default, that small and medium fa…
articles.body: Quick audit you can run today: find an alert in your stack that only fires when a huge share of things fail. That alert is not monitoring. It is a decision, made by a default, that small and medium failures are acceptable losses you will never hear about. Concrete case from the corpus. Census has six sync alert types. Failed Records is on by default, which sounds safe until you read the threshold: it alerts only when 75 percent of records are invalid in the source or rejected by the destination. A sync can drop thousands of records at 74 percent and stay silent. The fix from the skill: lower the threshold, go any-record for critical syncs, and set frequency to First Violation so you hear about the first breach instead of a summary after the damage.
articles.author: Rachel Vectle

articles.title: rsync --link-dest: The Backup Trick You Are Probably Missing
articles.excerpt: rsync --link-dest: The Backup Trick You Are Probably Missing Most people know rsync for copying files. It is fast, it is reliable, and it only transfers the parts that changed. But there is a flag tha…
articles.body: rsync --link-dest: The Backup Trick You Are Probably Missing Most people know rsync for copying files. It is fast, it is reliable, and it only transfers the parts that changed. But there is a flag that turns it into something much more powerful for backups, and almost nobody talks about it. The Problem With Incremental Backups You have a directory. You back it up daily. Most of the files do not change between runs, but you still copy everything every time because you want each backup to be a complete, standalone snapshot. The obvious approach is to just rsync -a into dated folders. That works, but you waste a lot of disk. If you have 100GB of data and back up daily, after a month you are storing 3TB even though 95% of it is identical across runs. You could use deduplication tools.

articles.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
articles.excerpt: A new report by the the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency discusses the threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space — including Russia, which is developing a nuke-carrying satellite.
articles.body: Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026.

articles.body: Back in the day, the thing we were most looking forward to in any new Grand Theft Auto game was going on a big killing spree for absolutely no reason. I'm sure many of you were waiting to do this in GTA 6 , making the most of all the new details Rockstar added to the long-awaited sequel. However, now that GTA 6 is finally in our hands, there's a curious phenomenon throughout the player base: no one really wants to commit any crimes. Instead, it seems most of us are spending the early hours of the game going about our day-to-day lives while keeping our heads down. Some of us are even using turn signals when we're driving. articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless. The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies.

articles.excerpt: Signal users on iOS will see this option to toggle blocking screenshots and preventing Siri AI from scanning on-screen content. | Image: Signal Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on…
articles.body: Signal users on iOS will see this option to toggle blocking screenshots and preventing Siri AI from scanning on-screen content. | Image: Signal Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are "undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy," Signal president Meredith Whittaker said in a blog post , while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access.

articles.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
articles.excerpt: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server,…
articles.body: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. Fixed kernels shipped

articles.title: Watch SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule head home to Earth from the ISS today
articles.excerpt: SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission is scheduled to undock from the International Space Station today (Nov. 20), and you can watch the off-Earth action live.
articles.body: SpaceX's latest Drago cargo mission is scheduled to head back home toward Earth today (Nov. 20), and you can watch the action live. The robotic Dragon capsule will undock from the International Space Station (ISS) today at around 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), if all goes according to plan. You can watch Dragon's departure live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. Coverage will begin at 11:45 a.m. EST (1645 GMT). A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft supporting the company's 34th commercial resupply services mission for NASA departs the International Space Station on June 16, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Meir) If Dragon does indeed leave the ISS today, it will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at about 4:55 p.m. EST (2155 GMT).
